ledger.claim: The threshold test runs on the GPS trace, not on the receipt's round number: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test. The trace records 22.40 km against the platform's own optimal of 17.60 km — an excess of 4.80 km, which is 27.3% of optimal and clears both the 20% test and the 0.80 km test — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 carries admissibility weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and that its distance figure is the fact this claim rests on.

The 13 minute 30 second conflict between the trip record's started_at (18:32:10) and the trace's first movement (18:18:40) does not take the rider's case down, because the driver's own account supplies the explanation: he states the app kept showing the trip as not started. A meter that started late leaves the trip record's started_at as the erroneous field and the continuous, gap-free trace as the reliable one; the 2.38 km the trace records before 18:32:10 is therefore distance driven on this trip, not the tail of a previous job, and the 22.40 km figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes govern. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so its 22.40 km is not reduced. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap of more than 90 seconds, a fix-to-fix jump of more than 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds; EV-GPS-00112 has max_gap_sec 0.0, an empty gaps array, 100% coverage of the recorded window and a 10-second sample interval, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. Its 0.4 multiplier is a POL-GEN-02 confidence discount only, and the schema-IMPAIRED tag is not the same thing as policy impairment. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The driver's account that he made the Paya Lebar Quarter stop is contradicted by the trace, so it exonerates nothing. The chat log's waypoint_hint resolves the rider's request to a real venue coordinate (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the closest the vehicle ever comes to that waypoint is 512.35 m — far outside the 200 m corroboration test POL-RD-04 requires — so although the instruction was the rider's, was timely and named a specific place, the corroboration limb fails. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes no distance at all: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no part of the excess is written off as a rider-requested detour, and the deviation stands at the measured figure. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT; EV-CHAT-00112 is complete at weight 1.0.

ledger.claim: This case cannot be closed as NO_ACTION with the charge left standing on the rider. The pickup timestamps on two admitted artifacts — the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10 and the trace's first fix of 18:18:40 — disagree by 13 minutes 30 seconds, which is over the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4); and independently the two artifacts that carry the excess, EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each sit at weight 0.4, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in any ruling that rests on them is capped at 0.4, below the 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10(1) makes an escalation trigger. On either footing the disputed amount is held pending human review rather than collected from the rider. I disclose that both artifacts are impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The deviation the rider complains of is not established once the trace is measured across the recorded trip. The recorded events on EV-TRIP-00112 are a pickup at 18:32:10 and a dropoff at 18:52:20, and POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance as the length of the gps_trace polyline between those two events. EV-GPS-00112 carries 2.38 km of movement between its first fix at 18:18:40 and that 18:32:10 pickup, before this trip began. Measured across the recorded trip window the distance driven is 20.02 km against a 17.6 km optimal route, an excess of 2.42 km or 13.8 per cent, which fails the 20 per cent establishment gate and, no deviation existing, makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The fork is on the face of the bundle: the assessor's own note on EV-GPS-00112 records that the whole-trace reading gives 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent while the reading from started_at gives 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, that this moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold, and that nothing in the bundle decides which interpretation is correct. The rider carries the initial burden of the threshold showing under POL-RD-08, and an excess left unresolved between 13.8 and 27.3 per cent does not discharge it. I disclose that both artifacts I cite are impaired: EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112 each carry issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and a weight_multiplier of 0.4.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider, where the whole 22.40 km trace governs and the deviation is established at 27.3 per cent, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic returns her nothing. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal minutes) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 optimal-route ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 25.64. Charged_total is 25.26. The refund is charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero: 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, so nil; and a nil refund is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, which POL-RD-02 makes NO_ACTION. The platform's own money block on EV-FARE-00112 says the same thing on its face: recomputed_fare 25.64, refund before rounding 0, quantum 0.05, payable 0.00. The rider was billed less on the distance and time lines than the optimal route would have cost her, so there is nothing on those lines to return.

This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider's maximum remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and never the uplift. POL-RD-01 makes a deviation material only where the excess exceeds 50 per cent of the optimal distance or 8.0 km absolute; the highest figure anywhere on this record is 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent, so neither limb is met, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is open. If the profile is consulted anyway because the evidence is finely balanced, the pattern test fails on its own two fields: EV-DPROF-00112 records deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296, a ratio of 0.003, below the 0.05 ratio POL-RD-06 sets and below the alternative count of 3. POL-GEN-01 confines that artifact to that test and no other field on it is cited here. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112, cited for the excess figures, carries issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight 0.4.

The trace is impaired at the schema layer and clean at the policy layer, and both statements must be made. The schema impairment is real and is disclosed: EV-GPS-00112 has status IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4, and it arises solely from its alignment with EV-TRIP-00112, not from any defect in the trace itself. The policy layer is clean, and the assessor says so on EV-GPS-00112: there is no gap (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), coverage_pct is 100.0 and the sampling interval is a steady 10.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires and the corroboration requirement and escalation consequences in POL-RD-10(3) are not triggered. Under POL-GEN-02 the down-weight caps confidence in whatever the ruling rests on, but it does not convert a policy-clean trace into one from which a deviation cannot be established, and the two findings must be stated side by side.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09 to be added on top of anything. EV-FARE-00112 itemises erp_gantries as empty, tolls_erp at 0.00, airport_surcharge at 0.00 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, and waiting_time_fee at 0.00. Its admissibility assessment records that the line items reconcile to the cent: 3.80 base fare + 15.00 distance + 5.66 time + 0.80 platform fee = 25.26. There is no off-route gantry and no phantom line, so no standalone pass-through refund and no billing-integrity finding arises.

In the alternative, on the reading that POL-RD-01's governing-field sentence prefers - the gps_trace figure governs the distance - the driver was under-billed rather than the rider overcharged. EV-FARE-00112 bills distance_charged_km of 20.00 while EV-GPS-00112 records trace_distance_km of 22.40, a shortfall of 2.40 km against the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04, so the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.40 x 0.75 = SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and far inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired, carrying issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4; the billed-distance side of the comparison is carried by EV-FARE-00112 at full weight.

The rider's second complaint, that the Paya Lebar Quarter stop she asked for was not made, cannot found a refund on this fare. EV-FARE-00112 charges nothing for a stop and nothing for waiting: waiting_time_fee is 0.00, there are no fixed surcharges on the trip, and the platform fee is a flat 0.80; the only lines POL-RD-02 recomputes are the distance and time charges, and those are what the rider's own figures put in issue. She paid no charge for the stop she says she did not get, so that limb of the claim adds nothing to any amount the distance lines could produce.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded (POL-RD-10; POL-GEN-03).

Why it cannot be finally decided. The two artifacts that measure this trip cannot agree when it began. EV-TRIP-00112 puts the pickup/start at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112 begins at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that moment. That is a 13 minute 30 second disagreement, beyond the 10-minute limb in POL-RD-10(4), and it decides the threshold test: read over the whole trace the trip is 22.40 km against a 17.6 km optimal, an excess of 4.80 km / 27.3% that clears POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates and establishes a deviation; read from the recorded started_at only 20.02 km was driven, an excess of 2.42 km / 13.8% that fails them. The admissibility report itself records that nothing in the bundle decides which reading is correct. The driver's account that the app kept showing the trip as not started is an assertion that does not dissolve a contradiction the policy makes its own escalation ground, and on the other point he is contradicted by the trace.

Confidence. The deciding fact — the start-time conflict — is carried only by EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, each rated weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at 0.4. That is below the 0.70 floor, which also triggers POL-RD-10(1) on its own. I record that this is schema-level impairment, not policy-level impairment: under POL-RD-07 the trace is clean (no gap over 90 s, no fix-to-fix jump over 500 m, a steady 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and I do not treat the trace as unusable for policy purposes.

For the reviewer, the arithmetic if a deviation is established. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal fare at 25.64 — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from EV-FARE-00112, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, surcharge or waiting charge — against the 25.26 charged, leaving a refund of nil, below the 0.50 de minimis. The driver's claim to SGD 1.80 for 2.40 unbilled km under POL-RD-04 rests on the same contested trace figure and likewise cannot be resolved here. There is no off-route ERP, toll, surcharge or phantom line to correct under POL-RD-09, and no POL-RD-06 referral: the deviation is not material (27.3% and 4.80 km are below the 50% and 8.0 km limbs) and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 296 completed trips establishes no pattern.

The Paya Lebar Quarter complaint adds nothing to any amount. The rider's request and the driver's 'ok can' are in EV-CHAT-00112, but the trace never comes within the 200 m corroboration test (nearest fix 512.35 m from the waypoint), so under POL-RD-14 the instruction is uncorroborated, excludes no distance, and no charge was levied for the stop in any event. No corroboration uplift applies to this rider under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0), and no traffic advisory covers the trip window (EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), so no external-cause exoneration arises.

What would resolve it on review: a record fixing when this trip truly started — a meter or booking log showing the meter start, or a GPS export placing the trace's first 2.38 km in a prior job — would let the excess be measured on a single window and end the dispute.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
